extracted.intended_audience: psychoanalysts, psychologists, scholars and students of humor and literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Theoretical analysis of the psychic mechanisms, motives, forms, and social conditions of wit/jokes (jest, wit, tendency-wit), and how they produce pleasure and laughter. Focuses on criteria that make an utterance a jest vs wit and the interpersonal dynamics required for its success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two impulses directing wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit development is directed by two impulses: one striving to elude reason and the other to substitute for the adult an infantile state of mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dual impulses underlie the movement from play to jest to wit; they motivate the search for word- and thought-combinations that permit pleasure while evading rational prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the jest (Scherz)
rubrics_metrics.description: The jest's object is to bring about the resultant pleasure of playing while appeasing the protesting reason which strives to suppress the pleasant feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accomplished by senseless combinations or absurd linkings that 'must make sense after all.' Examples include harmless verbal parings (Kästner, Rokitansky). The jest employs technical means of wit but need not contain valuable or new content—only expressibility and the gratification of forbidden play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jest need not be novel or valuable
rubrics_metrics.description: The pith of a jest does not need to be valuable, new, or even good; it only matters that it can be expressed, even if obsolete or superfluous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A jest's chief factor is the gratification it affords by enabling what reason forbids; content may be unimpressive yet still pleasurable by virtue of word-play or sound-unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peculiar technique of wit: safeguarding pleasure against reason
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinct technique of wit consists in safeguarding pleasure-forming word- and thought-combinations against the protest of reason which would obviate the pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wit-makers select word-material and thought-situations so play survives rational criticism; this requires clever exploitation of linguistic peculiarities and mental constellations though the exact selection mechanism is not fully explicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense-in-nonsense requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: What appears nonsensical from one viewpoint must appear meaningful or acceptable from another; otherwise it is relegated to 'nonsense.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'sense in nonsense' allows the pleasurable play to pass the test of reason; if the wit-work fails to produce a reconciling sense, the effect collapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: jest vs wit (value of thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a jest's utterance is substantial and valuable it changes into wit: the thought that would be interesting in itself is invested in a form that excites additional satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wit magnifies and recommends the thought to attention and confuses reason; this fusion of good thought and witty form creates uncertainty about the pleasure's origin and increases perceived importance of the thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as service to tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is enlisted by psychic tendencies (exhibitionistic, aggressive, cynical, sceptical, obscene) to further their aims—overcoming inhibitions, shattering respect, or converting hearers into allies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: obscene wit overcomes shame; aggressive wit overthrows critical judgment and mobilizes listeners against an enemy; cynical/sceptical wit undermines institutions by strengthening argument and employing new attacks. Wit pushes aside reason as a more efficacious psychological route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendency-wit liberates repressed emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency-wit can free pleasure from sources that have undergone repression by removing inner inhibitions and making repressed tendencies available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not a simple propelling power but involves mechanisms like using wit-pleasure as a lever to access repressed material; examples and further mechanisms are developed with reference to repression and inner hindrances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of fore-pleasure (aesthetic assistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small wit-pleasure can act as an 'alluring premium' (fore-pleasure) that enables a suppressed tendency to break through, yielding a much larger resultant pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on Fechner's principle of aesthetic assistance: meeting of pleasurable factors can exceed the sum of parts. Example: words intended for an insult are reframed into wit, and the hinted insulting quality combines with the wit-pleasure to produce greater satisfaction and even allow the suppressed tendency to strengthen and overcome inhibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play-pleasure vs removal-pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit's pleasures are classifiable as play-pleasure (from free play with words/thoughts) and removal-pleasure (from removal of inhibitions/repressions), both traceable to economy of psychic expenditure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developmental sequence: play → jest → harmless wit → tendency-wit; as wit matures it opens new pleasure sources by removing inhibition while retaining original word-pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special talent or psychic disposition for wit-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit-making is not available to all; it appears as a fairly independent ability, somewhat separate from intelligence, memory, or imagination, and may be associated in some cases with neurotic or dissociated personalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Heine's 'famillionaire' rooted in personal history; Jewish witticisms reflecting self-participation; anecdotal observation that known wits sometimes show predisposition to nervous affections—though insufficient data to claim neurotic constitution is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition to display as motive for harmless wit
rubrics_metrics.description: A common motive for harmless wit is the ambitious impulse to display one's spirit or 'show off,' analogous to sexual exhibitionism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of numerous inhibited impulses increases tendency-wit production; certain sexual components (e.g., sadistic elements) may predispose individuals to particular forms of tendency-wit (aggression, obscenity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impulse to impart wit (social necessity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit-making is inseparably connected with the desire to impart it; unlike finding the comic alone, wit must be communicated to achieve its consummation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process of wit-formation often remains incomplete until other persons are present; originators commonly overcome objections to share wit, indicating an essential social dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of a third person for wit's completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The successful consummation of a jest/wit depends on a third person (the hearer) who decides its prosperity; this person must be in a jovial or indifferent state and free from strong opposing feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The third person is not merely an object but analogous to the 'other' in comic situations; absence of willingness or presence of antagonistic feelings (e.g., loyalty to the target) will prevent the joke from functioning as wit. Shakespeare: 'A jest's prosperity lies in the ear Of him that hears it.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions blocking third-person participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors that evoke strong opposing feelings in the third person (indignation, loyalty, decorum, aesthetic culture) block their readiness to laugh at a particular witticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context matters: certain audiences (e.g., an assemblage of clergy) will not accept smutty or insulting wit about someone they respect; the presence of the target's friends will shift perception from wit to invective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter as discharge of psychic energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter (especially laughter at wit) is a discharge of psychic irritation or dammed energy: when the psychic energy formerly used to occupy certain channels becomes unutilizable, it is discharged as laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modified Spencerian view: laughter results from a sudden transfer or release (descending incongruity/relief). For hearers, a forbidden idea introduced by the witticism allows dammed inhibition-energy to be released, producing pleasure; this accounts for why hearers laugh more explosively than originators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why the originator often does not laugh
rubrics_metrics.description: The creator of a witticism frequently cannot laugh at it because during conception either the suspension of inhibition energy or the discharge possibility was impeded—so the originator incurred psychic expenditure or inhibition that prevents discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whereas the hearer 'buys' the pleasure with little expenditure (economy of psychic effort), the originator expended energy in producing the thought and often remains inhibited during its formation; thus laughter/ discharge occurs more readily in the third person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearer's pleasure corresponds to economized psychic expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearer's laughter reflects liberation of inhibition-energy that otherwise would have required their own psychic expenditure to bring about; the pleasure equals the saved psychic work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hearer experiences a gratuitous release: the witticism produces an idea that for them would have been suppressed or difficult to form, and this sudden production allows immediate discharge through laughter.
